correctness.rationale: The upper bound follows from numerical-range inclusion in the spectral triangle. Strict positivity of the incenter Lagrange residues and their unit sum are proved by angle bisectors and polynomial interpolation. Their normal-vector compression has repeated eigenvalue c, hence disk-shaped 2D numerical range; three side-contact vectors force its radius exactly r. A trigonometric polynomial of degree at most two cannot have three distinct even-multiplicity zeros unless zero, proving the maximizing numerical-range set must be the incircle. Multiplicity and infinite-dimensional extension use three reducing eigenvectors. A symbolic 3–4–5 triangle verifies the identity exactly; finite tests corroborate but do not prove the general case. The block identity uses the source in its valid finite-matrix domain.

value.rationale: The elliptical width is a natural operator invariant defining a sharp quantitative positive-block norm correction. For the first noncollinear normal spectral class, the theorem computes it explicitly for every triangle and every spectral multiplicity, constructs the extremizing plane, and proves uniqueness of its disk numerical range. This is a complete structural classification rather than an arbitrary finite sample or a parameter increment. No broader operator-class formula is claimed.
